Xiaomi has been disobedient since childhood—when others say east, he insists on going west. 
His aunt always says it's because he was born on Grain in Ear, carrying a body full of prickly awns. 
Xiaomi retorts, "Then go talk to my parents! They gave me this name—what grain doesn’t have awns?" 
At the mention of his parents, his aunt falls silent, only muttering that she can’t argue with him and will send him to Jadecloud for schooling when he’s older, so Master Yuan can discipline him properly. 
Xiaomi doesn’t understand why his aunt clams up at the mention of his parents. He’s never met them and doesn’t know what use they’d be. All he knows is his aunt doesn’t want to raise him anymore—she wants to send him away. 
"I won’t go. What kind of name is 'Master Duck' or 'Master Chicken'? I won’t learn from someone with such an ugly name." 
"Ha ha, well said." 
"You—who are you? I’ve never seen you before. Stay back! My boleng drum is really powerful!" 
The man stands under the old locust tree by the gate, tall and lanky, like a stretched-out dot. 
Xiaomi grips his boleng drum and takes a few cautious steps back. 
"Don’t be afraid," the man says. "Your aunt said the mechanical ox stopped working again, so I came to check. Seems like you were the one who took apart the previous ones too?" 
"I—it wasn’t me! And I put them back together!" Xiaomi relaxes a little. 
"You did a good job," the man says, stepping inside only when Xiaomi seems less afraid. He crouches down to meet Xiaomi’s eyes. "Just a few parts were installed backward." 
"Says you! You’re not the Mohist Grandmaster!" 
The man laughs heartily before replying, "Whether I’m the Grandmaster doesn’t matter. But the ratchet you misassembled actually has 'front' and 'back' carved on it. If you’d learned to read, you wouldn’t have made that mistake." 
Xiaomi’s eyes dart around—he’s no fool. "Then I only need to learn those two words. What’s the point of reading when riding a mechanical ox through the mountains is way more fun?" 
"Hmm, fair point. What if you could ride a mechanical ox while reading and writing? Would you come to Jadecloud then?" 
"You—you’re Master Yuan? So this boleng drum… you made it?" 
"I did. And not just the drum—mechanical oxen, wooden kites, mechanical horses… I can make them all." 
"Then… I’ll learn from you!" 
……………… 
Spring passed, autumn came, and another Grain in Ear arrived. 
Xiaomi takes his boleng drum and mounts the mechanical ox. He’s heard—the seeds are in Jadecloud. He must return to protect Master’s seeds. If he misses Grain in Ear, he’ll miss this year’s planting season.
